text:
kate_pm: Quick sync — we need a concise acceptance checklist and decisions on pricing semantics for the quota/rate limiting work. Customers keep asking about fallback model billing and quota UI tradeoffs. Can we align today?

aj_eng: Yep. Main decision: bill per-token vs bill per-invocation (or hybrid). Per-token is fair but more complex for cached/fallback flows.

samir_research: From model side — fallbacks happen when primary model OOMs or cold start delays. We should define: when fallback happens, do we charge full primary tokens, fallback tokens, or the max? Also how to surface to customers for audits.

liam_billing: Prefer: metered units = actual tokens generated by the serving model. For primary->fallback we tag each response with "serving_model" and token_counts in the invoice log. If fallback was used we can include a transparency flag and optionally apply a negotiated discount.

jenna_support: Edge cases from support: partial responses (timeout mid-stream), client retries, and ambiguous errors where both models attempted. Need clear customer-facing language and an endpoint to fetch per-request billing metadata.

aj_eng: API sketch for minimal change: add response header and usage object in sync response: 

``` 
POST /v1/generate
Request: {model: "rwd-llama-70b", prompt: "..."}
Response headers:
  X-Rwd-Serving-Model: rwd-llama-70b
  X-Rwd-Tokens-Used: 254
Response body: {"id":"r-123","usage":{"tokens":254,"model":"rwd-llama-70b"}}
```

If fallback used: X-Rwd-Fallback: rwd-4o, usage.tokens should be per-serving-model and a top-level aggregated field.

kate_pm: Good. For the PRD acceptance criteria I propose the following minimal list: 
- Billing: invoices include per-request breakdown with model tag + token counts.
- API: response contains serving_model and tokens fields (backward compatible).
- UI: quota page shows both committed quotas and recent consumption by model + daily granularity.
- SLAs: fallback should not increase billed tokens beyond actual tokens generated; customers to opt-in for "charge-primary-if-fallback" during contract negotiation.
- Telemetry: traces capture route decisions (why fallback) and a rollout metric for % fallbacks.

samir_research: Add acceptance on correctness: KV-cache hits should not double-charge. If prefix cache returns cached tokens, tokens billed must reflect what was actually produced, not what was skipped.

liam_billing: Also need to specify data export CSV columns: request_ts, request_id, serving_model, fallback_model (nullable), tokens_generated, billed_units, customer_id. We'll enforce syntactic schema in billing export.

jenna_support: And add QA edge cases: aborted stream, client disconnect, 429 backoff + retry loop — we need to define which request gets billed. My recommendation: bill for completed tokens up to the point of abort; track original request_id and retries correlate.

aj_eng: Implementation notes: runtime will emit an event per response: {request_id, serving_model, tokens_produced, fallback_reason?}. We can reuse existing events bus but add new fields. Pseudocode: 
```
emit_event({request_id, serving_model, tokens: n, fallback: "oom"})
```
Billing consumer reads these, aggregates per-customer.

kate_pm: Scope negotiation: MVP = hosted API + billing export + simple UI view. Dedicated/Private parity tracked but out of scope for V1. We should ship canary to 10% of orgs with high usage.

liam_billing: Pricing semantics decision: default = per-token billing. For contract customers we support per-second or capacity reservation models (handled outside this flow). Documented in PRD.

samir_research: Acceptance must include regression tests: synthetic workload that triggers fallback and asserts billing rows. Also a test for caching path no double-charge.

jenna_support: Launch checklist input from Support: KB article, example billing queries (5 common searches), runbook for contested charges.

kate_pm: Rollout plan: 1) API + events (internal) -> 2) billing export + UI -> 3) canary customers -> 4) GA. Metrics to watch: billing_consistency_errors (0), fallback_rate, customer_support_tickets about charges, and time-to-sync between event emission and billing export.

aj_eng: One more: quota enforcement vs soft quota. We need acceptance: soft quota triggers warning and does not block; hard quota blocks with 429. UI should let customers pick their default.

liam_billing: Worth adding grace credit flow: if hard quota hit, allow manual override and show dispute flag on exported rows.

deploy-bot: canary config updated: product/canary-metering set -> 10% traffic at 2026-04-02T10:00Z

kate_pm: Ok, next steps: aj to draft API changes (open PR), liam to list billing export schema, samir to write regression tests, jenna to draft KB. I'll assemble PRD acceptance table after those are in. :thumbsup:

aj_eng: I'll drop the API PR by EOD and ping for review.

liam_billing: Will share schema + sample CSV by tomorrow morning.

samir_research: I'll add tests to the eval harness and link to PR.

jenna_support: I'll start a KB draft and paste into this thread when ready.

kate_pm: Thanks team — we'll reconvene after PRs land.
